sector_model: nonfinancial medical technology (musculoskeletal devices); use earnings, FCF, net cash, inventory and working capital, acquisition effects
thesis: Globus Medical sells spine and orthopedic implants and enabling technology. After a 12.8% one day fall to 71.05 (11-06) it trades near 16.9x TTM GAAP earnings and 8.1% TTM FCF yield with about 871M cash and marketable securities and no financial debt. 9M26 operating cash flow was 677M (+34%) and operating income 510M (+64%, partly lapping Nevro merger costs), a 500M buyback increase was authorized. The market is reacting to a cut in 2026 revenue guidance, not to a collapse in profit.
counterthesis: Revenue guidance was cut to 3.09B from 3.18-3.22B (about 3.5% below the old midpoint) and Q3 sales fell 0.7% (U.S. +0.5%, international -5.7%); U.S. Spine grew 2% against double digit comps, so share gain and growth claims are weakening. Base business (ex Nevro) grew only 3.0%. Revenue growth in 9M26 (+9.5%) is mostly Nevro acquisition. FCF is record partly because of tax payable timing (+17.5M vs -57.9M a year ago, a 75M swing) and receivables/inventory (inventory +60M) may signal channel strain; allowance for credit losses rose. TTM earnings include a 114.4M bargain purchase gain only through FY2025 comparisons and a low-tax quarter in 9M25 (tax rate 22% in 9M26 vs 8.8%). Non-GAAP EPS guidance 4.95-5.05 excludes amortization, restructuring and acquisition costs, and buybacks (279M 9M26) partly mask slow growth. Acquisition liabilities of 106M are debt-like.
invalidation: Another guidance cut or U.S. spine growth turning negative; gross margin gains reversing; inventory build without sales growth; Nevro integration impairment; FCF falling below net income once tax timing normalizes.
